title: Self-exile
subtitle: We were not exiled. We volunteered to build our homeland far away.

items.text: Self-exile

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: It's so ... desolate.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Compared to this place, Tobolsk is like the Leningrad of Siberia.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: There must be a bounty of untapped resources here.

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: I'd be more focused on finding a place to stay if I were you.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: In what direction is the nearest town? How far is it?

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: Town? There's nothing but prisons here, lad.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: ... Prisons?

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: You heard me. Not even a pigeon would stop to crap in this cesspit.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: So, where are these prisons?

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: You're in one, mate.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Ha! I get it. You're messing with me.

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: Tsk. You came all this way, and you don't even know a single thing about this place. You're dead meat.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: I just came here to investigate ...

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: Head south. Or buy another ticket and come back with us. That's my suggestion.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: I ... can't.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: When will your ship come back again?

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: Side barges are centrally managed ... It could be 15 days. Maybe longer.

items.speaker: Sailor
items.text: Until then, do your best to stay alive.
"The government journalist discovered the poems and stories while searching for shelter."
"They were written on pieces of wood, stones, and scattered parchment."
"Ecstatic at his discovery, the journalist set out to identify the author and collect them all."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Mr. Зима ... doesn't seem like someone who could handle something like that.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: If it weren't for these stone-paved roads, I swear, I would have marked this place as a "no man's land."
In an opening not far away, crude shacks, some empty or collapsed, stretch out like long scars torn into the earth.
At the center lies an extinguished campfire.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: What about those people who were exiled about a decade ago? Did they all escape?

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: In those surviving records, the end of the exile policy ...

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: But ... anyone who found themselves in this environment must have constantly thought of escaping.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Forget it. I'll look for traces of life first. Maybe I'll find ...

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Huh? The fire. It's still warm.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Is this ...?
Half-burned parchment is scattered around the campfire in a scene of attempted destruction. He picks up one sheet.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: ... Parchment paper with poetry on it and a still-smoldering campfire!

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Someone is definitely here!

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Who could it be? Who would write poetry in a place like this?
It is an amazing discovery. The next occurrence, however, is even more surprising.
A bird swoops over and snatches the parchment from his hand like an eagle plucking a fish from the ocean.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: ... Hey!

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: That's mine! I found it! You nasty little thing!

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Give it back!
Humans who neglect to exercise are no match for wild animals.
What this human now faces is a primitive yet most difficult-to-resist ambush.
Primitive, but efficient. It is orderly and prepared.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: What's going on!?

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: How are there so many ...!?
The birds, dedicated to driving off the intruder, give him no answer.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: *chirps*

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: P-please, let go of my clothes!

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Where are you taking me?

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: The parchment!? I don't want the parchment! Give me back my notebook ...

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: No! That's the brooch my mother left me!
In such chaos, opportunities are fleeting.
He must grab it and take back what is his!

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: You!

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Give it to me ... Let go!
This sudden surge of resistance deters the birds for a few seconds.
There is a brief pause in their attack. Then, a figure leisurely steps out of the woods.
Please ... ahem ... s-stop.
... *sigh*.
Sorry ...
... about ... your mother's brooch ...
TO BE CONTINUED…
